idiom_name: Spring Data keyset scrolling (Window + KeysetScrollPosition + WindowIterator)
implementation_notes: Spring Data provides the whole structure: declare Window<User> findFirst10ByLastnameOrderByFirstname(String lastname, KeysetScrollPosition position); keyset scrolling rewrites the query criteria to include the sort fields plus the primary key so the database seeks an index instead of materializing an offset, and WindowIterator.of(position -> repo.find(...)).startingAt(ScrollPosition.keyset()) applies the next position for you. When the cursor must cross the wire, encode Window.positionAt(size - 1) with your own token codec; without Spring Data the classic JPQL WHERE (createdAt, id) < (:ts, :id) form remains the fallback.
pitfalls: Keyset scrolling requires non-nullable sort properties: NULL comparison semantics break the criteria rewrite, and every sorted property must be mapped in the returned entity or DTO projection or keyset extraction fails.
ScrollPosition.offset() (the start marker) differs from offset(0L) (which, because positions are exclusive, skips the first element) - a classic off-by-one when hand-writing the first request.
